<result>Nothing is merged or completed yet, and four of the five items are open. The first (B7b3b4cf483) is waiting on a rerun of the `ci` gate after a one-test failure. LS-measure is blocked on a fifth-round review the lead can unblock.

## LS-measure (the doctor line, `B-doctor-no-session-start-cost`)
- **Fix:** `ddflow doctor` now prints `session start cost: N tokens (budget M)`, with a per-part breakdown. It currently reads about 30.7K tokens against a 40K budget. The estimate counts the MCP instructions, `tools/list` for the active profile and the plain brief.
- **Knobs:** three new knobs, `[session].context_budget_tokens`, `start_bytes_per_token` and `start_notice_reserve_tokens`. A ratchet test is in `tests/test_session_start_budget.py`.
- **Where:** the code is in `ddflow/services/startcost.py` and `ddflow/surfaces/startcost_texts.py`.
- **Notice reserve:** measuring cannot count the once-per-version upgrade notice without using it up. So it adds a 100-token reserve instead, and a test shows the real notice fits.
- **Blocked on the fifth round:** `rubber_duck` ran a fifth round under your authorization. Three of its four findings I refuted: they repeat the notice-reserve point as a hypothetical 1,200-token notice that ddflow cannot emit. The fourth is real (the `chars` field actually held bytes). I fixed it by renaming the field to `bytes`.
- **What is still needed:** a delta review of that one commit (`start cost: bytes are called bytes`), or an operator waiver. `ddflow review triage` refuses to record the pass until the changed files are reviewed, and I will not exceed five rounds.
- **Still to run:** the `ci` and `unit_tests` gates, plus `bug_hunt` and `dedupe`. `critic` passed on refutation.
- **Fold:** `fix-B-doctor-no-session-start-cost` should be folded into LS-measure when it merges.
- **Glob release:** I already released the hot-file globs (`mcp.py`, README, golden and transcript files) from LS-measure.

## 1. B7b3b4cf483, progress heartbeat
- **Cause:** every offloaded tool except `review`, `merge`, `pins` and `upgrade` sent no progress, so Claude Code aborted a silent call.
- **Fix:** a new `ddflow/surfaces/mcp_heartbeat.py` sends a `notifications/progress` every `[mcp].progress_s` seconds (default 20, 0 turns it off) for all seven `OFFLOADED` tools.
- **Deviation:** I did not set `wants_progress` on the six tools. That flag makes the registry pass `on_progress` to each tool's API, and these APIs take none. The heartbeat sits in `Server._call_api` instead.
- **Related changes:** progress now uses one lock-protected counter per call, scalar tokens only, and a locked worker frame writer.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_mcp_progress_all.py` has 24 cases, including an end-to-end run through the worker process. The original probes failed 7 of 7 before the fix.
- **Review:** `rubber_duck` passed (2 rounds) and `critic` passed on refutation. `standards` and `bug_hunt` are recorded.
- **Unreviewed commits:** the last four commits (`mcp: scalar progress tokens only, locked worker writes`, `mcp: one progress-token reader` and two test commits) were not seen by `critic`. `rubber_duck` saw the earlier commits only.
- **Remaining:** the full-suite `ci` gate failed on one test, `tests/test_worktree_adoption.py::test_adopt_existing_false_restores_the_old_behaviour`. It passes alone, so I read it as a load flake. The rerun is still to be done, then `unit_tests`, merge and complete.
- **Fold:** `RM-progress-everywhere` is not yet folded into the fix task; I did that deliberately only after merge.

## 4. B305db5608b, pins precheck and gate reasons
- **Fix (a):** `CI.run` now checks the pins in the merged tree first and fails at once with `pins stale after merging <base>: re-record them (…)`. It is controlled by a new knob `[ci].pins_precheck` (default true).
- **Fix (b):** `gate status` now shows the recorded reason for `unavailable` and `partial` gates, in a new `why` field. A reason that was empty or whitespace reads as "no reason was recorded".
- **Code moves:** `CI.run` was over the complexity ratchet, so I extracted `_unfinished`, which is behavior-preserving. The reasons code lives in the new `ddflow/services/gates/reasons.py`. I added `WHY_CHARS` to `docs/ddflow/constants-exemptions.toml`.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_ci_pins_precheck.py` has 11 cases; 3 failed on the old code.
- **Review:** `rubber_duck` passed after 3 rounds, `critic` passed on refutation, and `standards` is recorded.
- **Commits a reviewer did not see:** the last two (`ci precheck: say when it could not run; tests for the custom command`, then `ci precheck: a stale pin is named beside a run-wide problem; None reason`), plus the test commits after them.
- **Remaining:** the `ci` gate is queued behind the machine-wide suite lock. Then `unit_tests`, merge and complete.
- **What I did not find:** the "killed wrapper records unavailable with no reason" half of the bug was already fixed on main (`B58842554a7` records a reason). The gap was only the status display.

## 2 and 3. Not started
`B8f41346d9f` (the `ref=HEAD` problem) and `B-ci-run-item-id-branch-gone` both edit `ddflow/api/cirun.py`. That file is leased to fx-hand-record on `fix-Bed643a611b` for over 14 hours, so I could not claim them. My plan, once the file is free:
- **2:** make a missing `ref` mean "no ref" instead of defaulting to `"HEAD"`, so an explicit `ref=HEAD` is honored.
- **3:** when an item's branch is gone, fall back to its `merged_sha`.

- `ci.timeout_s = 7200` and `ci.suite_wait_s = 14400` are set in the shared `[REDACTED:path]`. Every worktree reads it. Please revert after my runs.

- Leases for LS-measure, `fix-B305db5608b` and `fix-B7b3b4cf483` need a heartbeat every 15 minutes or so, and I am not renewing them while idle. A background chain still runs `ci` and `unit_tests` for B305, then LS-measure. If the lead resumes me I will continue from there.

## Defects filed
- **`B-ci-suite-lock-wait-reason-generic`:** an unavailable verdict caused by the suite lock records only `exit 2 is declared UNAVAILABLE`; the real "blocked on pid N" line sits in the evidence tail.
- **`B-gate-run-ci-timeout-under-load`:** there is no per-run timeout override for `gate run ci`.
- **Not filed:** the hook refuses `ddflow review … --gate X --force` because it only allows `--force` right after the item id. It also lists the item-id-first ordering as the only exception, which the lead's instruction did not match. Please add a defect task for this.</result>

<result>Research and decision docs are merged to main; `P-commit-messages` (18 tasks) is queued and held behind the core/docs wave. Nothing is pushed. `CM-research` is completed, the worktree is clean and nothing is ahead of main. The roborev standards review found no issues, and its reviewer is a different model family from mine. Several claims in the research are marked unverified; the probe-first list is in section 10.

**Findings**
- ddflow generates about 14 kinds of commit text. The inventory is in research section 6; the only existing template is `[log].commit_events_message`. The hard-coded sentence in `agent_brief.md:44` is policy text, not a template.
- ddflow has no signing code (no `-S` anywhere).
- Probe: `git commit-tree` ignores `commit.gpgsign`, so ddflow's plumbing commits need an explicit `-S`.
- Probe: an SSH-signed commit verifies with `git verify-commit` and `%G?`. A hook in the primary `.git/hooks` also runs for commits made in linked worktrees.
- `jinja2` is a runtime dependency and a sandbox already exists in the export renderer. `ddflow record <kind>` already gives add/edit/remove/revise/history for any data kind.

**Design in brief**
- **Split:** context, template and policy are separate. The policy is the contract and a pure-stdlib lint enforces it; a template is just one producer and must pass the merged policy.
- **Contexts:** 19 built-in (task, fix, merge, events, release_*, housekeeping, port, pr_title, …), plus user-defined `[[commit.context]]` and `[commit.vars]`.
- **Layers:** the existing `D-config-layer-order`. Policy is tighten-only (unions, minimum of maxima, conjunction of regexes, maximum of sign mode). A lower layer may replace a template but its output is still linted.
- **Storage:** data kinds `commit_template` and `commit_policy`, a `[commit]` knob section, and the `[enforce]` trailer knobs kept as aliases.
- **Rendering:** sandboxed Jinja with a curated read-only context. The agent supplies fields and has at most 2 redrafts; no model runs in a hook.
- **Lint doors:** the commit-msg hook, ddflow's own messages in process (so `--no-verify` can't skip it), a new `commits` gate, and the pre-commit framework hook.
- **Signing:** `[commit].sign` is off/auto/required with scope merge/tips/all. ddflow verifies but never holds keys, and "cannot sign" is exit 2. `Signed-off-by` is a person's act.
- **Push:** `[commit].push` defaults to never, with protected branches, one guard on every ddflow push, and an optional generated `pre-push` hook (advisory).
- **MCP, no new tool:** template CRUD uses the existing `ddflow_record` and config uses `ddflow_configure`, both with no schema change. Four evaluator actions (`commit_render`, `commit_lint`, `commit_test`, `commit_status`) and five optional params are added to the existing `doctor` family. The byte cost is an unverified estimate.
- **By prompt:** a `commit-policy` workflow command prompt; every change is a recorded event and can be reviewed or restored.
- **Packs:** company packs travel in the org bundle, pinned by digest, data only; a bare URL is refused.

**Queued**
- **Phase and holds:** `P-commit-messages` needs `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap` and `P-docs-search`. The P-gaps core is already done.
- **Tasks:** CM-decide, CM-sandbox, CM-inventory, CM-config, CM-render, CM-lint, CM-sign, CM-push, CM-cli, CM-mcp, CM-prompt, CM-packs, CM-migrate-merge, CM-migrate-housekeeping, CM-migrate-release, CM-e2e, CM-docs.
- **Differences from your list:** I added CM-sandbox, which extracts one shared Jinja environment factory, because prompts, export and the planned CE-jinja each set up a sandbox. CM-migrate is split in three to keep globs small. The `commits` gate lives in CM-sign rather than CM-lint.
- **Dependencies:** CM-cli needs `MTD-family-spec`; CM-mcp needs `MTD-family-spec`, `MTD-family-schema` and `MTD-profiles`; CM-packs needs `B-org-kinds` and `B-org-policy`.
- **Checks:** the dependency graph has no cycles and my tasks' globs don't overlap each other. Several tasks share hot files with queued tasks and a few running fix items, for example `worktree.py`, `enforce.py` and `eventcommit.py`; the claim guard serialises those, and I didn't touch tool-diet, lean-start, soft-upgrade or fx-* files. `CM-migrate-merge` waits for `CM-push` because both edit `worktree.py`, and `CM-migrate-release` waits for it for `flow.py`.
- **Links:** the phase is related to P-requirements, P-id-consistency, P-agent-lifecycle, P-org-config, P-config-engine and P-tool-diet. Some tasks are linked to specific tasks in those phases.

**Open questions**
`CM-decide` holds Q1–Q13 with recommended defaults; the lead asks you.
- Most likely to change the design: MCP family (recommended `doctor`), and layer order. `D-config-layer-order` puts user *below* project, while you wrote "project, user, company". I followed the decision.
- The rest: default style, signing default, sign-off, push default, redraft bound, URL packs, the Item trailer for this project, audit-then-enforce, `[enforce]` aliases, subject limit.

**Filed defects**
- **B9834dabc40 (low):** a large listing piped to `head -1` makes the CLI exit 1 with a `BrokenPipeError` traceback. Reliable repro: `ddflow list task --state open --limit 1000 | head -1`. The stored repro-cmd (`ddflow show P-requirements | head -1`) does not reproduce on small output; I added a session note with the working one.
